messages:
alex: Heads up — alert firing: remote_write latency and 504s to long-term storage. Grafana shows write errors spiking at 11:40 UTC and unique series jumped from ~1.2M to ~3.8M in ~10m. Not sure if it's a recent deploy or scrape relabeling change.

mira: saw that too. Prometheus logs show: 
```
level=error ts=2024-04-15T11:40:12.345Z caller=remote.go:275 component=remote error="unexpected status code 504: gateway timeout"
```
Seems remote_timeout wasn't hit but the gateway returned 504s. Queue backpressure in prometheus is up.

sam: quick check — did we roll out any new sidecar or injector that adds high-card labels? I noticed a new image-build webhook last night.

jia: looking at series cardinality delta: labels with name "git_rev" and "build_sha" exploded across many pods; those were added by the new init container that writes env var to pod annotations. That'll create per-deploy series.

alex: nice find. So root cause = label cardinality spike from pod-level labels ending up on metrics via relabeling/service monitor. Two remediation tracks: 1) immediate protect remote_write/backend by increasing queue and timeout and adding write_relabel_configs to drop these labels; 2) fix ServiceMonitor/relabel_configs in k8s to stop scraping those labels into metrics.

mira: for quick mitigation I'm proposing to patch Prometheus remote_write config (prometheus-operator's Prometheus CR) with these lines:
```
remote_write:
- url: https://longterm-remote.example.com/api/v1/receive
  remote_timeout: 60s
  queue_config:
    capacity: 25000
    max_shards: 200
    min_shards: 1
    max_samples_per_send: 500
  write_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: ["git_rev", "build_sha", "commit"]
    action: labeldrop
```
This will drop the high-card labels at the send stage.

sam: +1. Also add a write_relabel rule to drop metrics we absolutely don't need in long term (e.g., per-pod ephemeral debug counters). We should be careful not to drop things used by SLOs.

jia: I'll make a PR for the prometheus-operator change. For the longer term we should patch ServiceMonitors to avoid relabeling pod annotations into target labels. Example relabel_config to drop the pod annotation label:
```
relabel_configs:
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape_id]
  action: drop
```
or to drop any label that matches the build/commit pattern.

mira: Also, metric_relabel_configs can remove labels from existing metrics before they create new series. Eg on ServiceMonitor: 
```
metric_relabel_configs:
- regex: "(git|build|commit)"
  action: labeldrop
  source_labels: [__name__]
```
(not exact syntax — will draft precise yaml in PR).

devops-bot: alert: PrometheusRemoteWriteErrors firing (threshold: >5% errors over 2m) in cluster-1. Incident page: https://incidents/redwood/1234

alex: For alerting noise: we'll suppress immediate pagers by increasing the alert window to 10m for the remote_write error pager and add an annotation to route to on-call only if error rate remains >10% for 20m. We still want dashboards to show the spike.

sam: ops checklist: 
- [ ] Patch Prometheus CR with write_relabel_configs + remote_timeout (canary one prometheus replica first)
- [ ] Add temporary queue capacity bump
- [ ] PR to ServiceMonitors to drop pod/build labels at target relabel stage
- [ ] Add metric_relabel_configs for long-term retention filter (labeldrop)
- [ ] Update alert thresholds to reduce flash pagers
- [ ] Run a backfill check on long-term storage after errors subside

jia: I'll open the PR to prometheus-operator now and target canary prometheus in prod-us-east-1. Putting draft here: https://git.company/redwood/ops/PR/4567 (will include exact relabel entries and test plan).

mira: small gotcha — labeldrop in write_relabel_configs only affects labels attached to samples being sent. If these labels are used by downstream queries/alerts in the short term, removing them will change query results. We should coordinate with any teams relying on those labels.

alex: good point. I've pinged infra-apps to see if they rely on git_rev/build_sha. They replied "we only used build_sha for one debug panel, can remove".

sam: after the canary patch, watch for queue length, send_success_rate, and remote_write_latency. Also watch prometheus TSDB memory — too many series previously caused increased memory churn.

devops-bot: deployment started: prometheus-prod-canary (image: prom-2.44.0) at 11:55 UTC.

jia: canary is up. Early metrics: remote_write 504s reduced but still some timeouts. I'll increase remote_timeout to 90s if we still see backpressure.

mira: once we confirm canary good for 30m, we'll roll to remaining replicas. Also schedule a follow-up to review relabeling hygiene and add a pre-deploy check for new labels on pods (CI job to fail if pods expose labels matching /commit|git_rev|build_sha/).

alex: thanks all. Action owners: jia - PRs and canary rollout; sam - alert tuning; mira - ServiceMonitor changes; I'll coordinate postmortem and update runbook.

sam: FYI I'll add a Grafana panel to show "new series per minute" and label cardinality top-10 to make future surges easier to triage.

mira: +1. Also adding a SLO for "scrape_success_rate" at 99.5% with burn alert to avoid silent regressions.

alex: closing the thread when postmortem PR is up. For now keep monitoring.
